clues.text: This place lies on flat land near a river in the middle of the country. An old famed road, Route 66, runs right through it.
clues.narrowing: Puts the player on a flat river plain in the middle of the country, on Route 66.

source.quote: The city lies in a plain near the Sangamon River north of Lake Springfield and is located along historic Route 66

clues.text: Hot, wet summers and cold, snowy winters both hit this place. It sits at the far edge of Tornado Alley, so strong storms roll through in the warm months.
clues.narrowing: Rules out mild coasts; keeps the stormy middle of the country.

source.quote: Hot, humid summers and cold, rather snowy winters are the norm. Springfield is located on the farthest reaches of Tornado Alley , and as such, thunderstorms are a common occurrence throughout the spring and summer

clues.text: The seat of government moved here in 1839, drawn by its spot at the center of the state. Local lawmakers worked hard to win the move here.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to seats of government won by a move to the center in 1839.

source.quote: Largely on the efforts of Lincoln and other area lawmakers, as well as its central location, Springfield was made the state capital in 1839

clues.text: Abraham Lincoln lived in this town for 24 years. In 1861 he left it to be President.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one famed president lived here for 24 years first.

source.quote: The most famous historic resident was Abraham Lincoln, who lived in Springfield from 1837 until 1861, when he became President of the United States

clues.text: The lawmakers of Illinois meet in this place to make state laws. The governor of Illinois keeps an office here too.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the state lawmakers and the governor are based here.

source.quote: State government institutions include the Illinois General Assembly, the Illinois Supreme Court, the office of the Governor of Illinois

reveal.blurb: Settlers built the first cabin here in 1820, by a creek full of deer and game. Abraham Lincoln moved here in 1837, worked as a lawyer, and helped win it the capital in 1839. His old home and tomb still draw crowds today. Springfield is the capital of Illinois.
